headline: Google Gemini Gems are being replaced by Skills in November
summary: Google is migrating its Gemini Gems feature to a more robust 'Skills' system, offering enhanced functionality and integration across chat windows.
details: Google is phasing out its Gemini Gems feature, which allows users to save custom prompts and formatting, replacing it with a more powerful 'Skills' system starting November 17, 2026.

Skills, similar to those found in other AI assistants like Claude, will offer a more integrated experience. Users will be able to invoke skills using a '/skill' command in any chat window, unlike the current Gems which require navigation to a dedicated section.

The new Skills system promises greater flexibility, allowing for the use of multiple skills within a single prompt and the ability to invoke one skill from another for complex tasks. This marks a significant upgrade from the current limitations of Gems.

Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers will have access to Skills, but it remains unclear how the transition will impact free Gemini users, as Gems are currently available to all users regardless of their subscription plan.

The migration to Skills is expected to coincide with the potential release of Gemini 4, which could bring further performance and efficiency improvements, potentially narrowing the gap with competitors like ChatGPT and Claude.

headline_marked: [[Apple Pay checkout]] gets a redesign in iOS 27 for easier card switching
headline: Apple Pay checkout gets a redesign in iOS 27 for easier card switching
summary: iOS 27 introduces a revamped Apple Pay experience with a new card picker and more payment details visible at a glance, streamlining the checkout process.
details: iOS 27 brings a significant overhaul to the Apple Pay interface, aiming to make transactions smoother and more intuitive for users.
The updated design features an easier way to switch between payment cards directly within the checkout flow. A new card picker allows for quick selection of preferred payment methods.
Users will also benefit from seeing more payment details at a glance, providing greater clarity on transaction information before confirmation.
This redesign focuses on enhancing the user experience for everyday purchases made through Apple Pay, whether online or in apps.
